definition: Autophagy is a biological process in which a cell encloses and breaks down parts of its own cytoplasm using structures such as autophagosomes, vacuoles, or multivesicular bodies, followed by digestion in lysosomes. It helps with normal body changes and tissue remodeling, and problems in this process are linked with some diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders and cancer.
